./.omo/ulw-research/20260814-040838/session-journal.md:31:- 원격 console/display socket은 서로 다른 BFF와 server-assigned topic ACL을 사용하고, display credential로 private topic 구독 시 403이 되는 통합 테스트를 필수로 한다.

./.omo/ulw-research/20260814-040838/session-journal.md:36:- pairing QR에 secret을 담을지, 인증된 device-authorization transaction만 담을지는 상충해 skeptic 반론으로 넘겼다.
./.omo/ulw-research/20260814-040838/session-journal.md:38:- session credential은 Account/PresentationControl/Device/AudienceDisplay 네 종류의 opaque host-only cookie로 나누고, role 변경·handoff·종료 시 회전/폐기하며 WSS도 즉시 닫는다.

./.omo/ulw-research/20260814-040838/SYNTHESIS.md:9:초기 결론은 **하나의 PWA 코드베이스, 두 개의 표시 모드, 서버 권한으로 분리된 세 화면 역할**이다. Windows 확장 화면에서는 Window Management API를 progressive enhancement로 사용해 공개 발표 창을 외부 디스플레이에 배치하고 Presenter Console을 주 화면에 둔다. 이 API는 실험적이며 Baseline이 아니므로, 권한 거부나 미지원 시 사용자가 창을 직접 옮기는 폴백을 제품의 정식 흐름으로 제공해야 한다.
./.omo/ulw-research/20260814-040838/SYNTHESIS.md:11:화면 복제 환경에서는 같은 머신에 콘솔을 띄우면 청중에게 그대로 노출되므로, 발표 머신에는 공개 화면만 유지하고 휴대폰·태블릿·노트북이 QR/코드로 Presenter Console 세션에 참여하도록 한다. 두 화면은 브라우저끼리 직접 신뢰하는 구조가 아니라 서버가 역할별 인증과 메시지 계약을 강제하는 세션 허브를 통해 동기화한다.
./.omo/ulw-research/20260814-040838/SYNTHESIS.md:30:- 공개 화면과 Presenter Console은 UI 라우트만 나누지 말고 역할별 서버 topic과 최소 DTO를 사용해야 한다. [S-01][S-14]
./.omo/ulw-research/20260814-040838/SYNTHESIS.md:58:1. 신청서 p7은 `SUPPORTED`를 공개 가능 상태로 설명하지만 p10은 발표자/팀 승인 후 표시한다고 한다. 해결안은 `evidence_status=SUPPORTED`와 `publication_status=APPROVED`를 분리하는 것이다.

content.text:
## Epistemic instrumentation

- `intent-diff.md`: 화면 모드와 공개 경계의 기대 사실을 추적한다.
- `claim-graph.md`: 브라우저 API, 원격 동기화, 공개 게이트 주장을 추적한다.
- `observation-manifest.md`: 신청서와 공식 문서 관찰을 독립 그룹으로 기록한다.

## Debate record

진행 중.

## Contradictions

1. 신청서 p7은 `SUPPORTED`를 공개 가능 상태로 설명하지만 p10은 발표자/팀 승인 후 표시한다고 한다. 해결안은 `evidence_status=SUPPORTED`와 `publication_status=APPROVED`를 분리하는 것이다.
2. Window Management API는 요구에 정확히 맞지만 Baseline이 아니다. 따라서 핵심 기능이 아니라 자동 배치 향상 기능으로만 사용한다.

## Gaps

- 2026년 브라우저별 실제 지원표와 설치형 PWA 동작 검증
- 원격 콘솔의 WebSocket/WebRTC 선택과 reconnect 상태 머신
- STT 공급자별 한국어 지연·정확도 실측

## Expansion trace

- Wave 0: PDF 전수 추출, 페이지 렌더링, 요구·도식 분석.
- Wave 1: 8명 연구팀 + 9개 독립 lane으로 PWA, 화면 모드, AI 파이프라인, 보안, UX, 경쟁 서비스, 반론 조사.

# Session Journal

## 2026-08-14 Wave 0

- PyMuPDF로 17쪽 텍스트와 이미지 메타데이터를 추출했다.
- 전체 페이지를 접촉 시트로 렌더링해 구조도, 상태도, 표를 육안 검토했다.
- 핵심 요구를 브리프와 intent diff에 기록했다.
- 코드베이스에는 PDF 외 파일이 없어 greenfield 구현 계획으로 분류했다.

## 2026-08-14 Wave 1 - realtime-ai 중간 관찰

- 신청서는 상시 LLM이 아니라 확정 발화와 현재 `slide_id`가 결합된 이벤트 기반 호출을 명시한다.
- 부분 STT는 자막과 검색 예열에만 사용하고 공개 카드 생성에는 쓰지 않는다.
- 공개 조건은 `SUPPORTED` 검증과 발표자/팀 승인이라는 서로 다른 두 개의 게이트로 해석해야 한다.
- 카드에는 `STALE`, `SUPERSEDED` 수명 상태가 필요하고, 미검증 상태는 청중 화면으로 절대 전달하지 않는다.
- security-privacy는 단순 라우트 분리가 부족하다고 지적했다. 공개 화면은 별도 origin·topic·최소 DTO를 사용하고, 비공개 데이터를 DOM에 숨겨 전달하는 방식을 금지해야 한다.
- pwa-platform 반론 결과 UI 별도 origin은 BroadcastChannel, opener, service worker lifecycle을 깨뜨린다. 결론은 same-origin UI route + 역할별 서버 topic/DTO/권한이다.
- remote-console은 WSS relay를 기본으로 하고 ICE/TURN·signaling이 필요한 WebRTC는 선택적 fast path로 제한하라고 권고했다.
- 5초 목표는 공개 SLA가 아니라 Presenter Console의 최대 3개 추천 SLA로 해석되었다.
- origin 경계는 재논쟁 상태다. same-origin은 BroadcastChannel/SW 조정이 쉽지만, 보안팀은 쿠키·localStorage·공개 SW 격리를 위해 별도 origin을 요구한다. WSS relay를 기준 통신으로 삼으면 공개 창과 콘솔이 BroadcastChannel을 공유할 필요가 없으므로 별도 origin이 유력하다.
- stack-economics는 Vite+React PWA, Supabase(Postgres/pgvector/Auth/Realtime/Storage), Deepgram Nova-3, OpenAI API의 월 $0 MVP를 제안했다. 다만 가격·무료 한도는 시점 의존이며 한국어 STT 정확도와 Supabase 휴면 복구를 실측해야 한다.
- origin 논쟁은 보안 우선으로 수렴했다. `app.example`(setup/controller/presenter)와 `stage.example`(public display)를 분리하고 WSS만 data plane으로 사용한다.
- controller는 cross-origin stage를 대상 화면 좌표에 열 수 있지만 stage DOM에 접근할 수 없다. stage fullscreen은 stage 화면에서 한 번 클릭해야 하므로 setup wizard의 명시 단계가 된다.
- 내부 RAG principal은 인증 서버에서 도출하고 Postgres RLS로 default-deny한다. 검색 엔진의 문자열 필터만 authorization으로 취급하지 않는다.
- 원격 콘솔 QR에는 credential을 넣지 않는다. 128-bit pair_id, 90초 TTL, 양 기기 동일 확인 문자열, 기존 콘솔의 명시 승인, 단일 사용 후 새 presentation-scoped device session 발급 흐름을 사용한다.
- Supabase Edge Functions는 Deno/TypeScript 전용이므로 python-pptx/LibreOffice 전처리를 둘 수 없다. MVP는 로컬 Python 업로더, 다중 사용자 단계는 Cloud Run Python worker가 최소 경로다.
- 확장 모드 1클릭 최적 흐름은 launcher를 외부 stage로 fullscreen하고 내부 화면에 console popup을 여는 것이다. console을 그대로 둔 채 cross-origin child stage를 열면 stage에서 fullscreen 1회 클릭이 추가된다.
- 브라우저 capability tier를 정의했다: Tier 0 수동 drag/fullscreen+WSS, Tier 1 Chromium desktop 자동 placement, Tier 2 설치형 standalone+offline shell. 설치는 멀티스크린 권한을 늘리지 않는다.
- cross-origin launch 최종 흐름은 setup permission과 popup activation을 분리한다: 권한 확인 후 `Open audience display` 클릭으로 `noopener,noreferrer` stage를 배치하고, stage 자체 클릭으로 fullscreen한다. WSS presence가 liveness source다.
- Presentation API는 Cast/TV adapter 후보지만 attached Windows monitor의 deterministic geometry를 주지 못해 핵심 폴백에서 제외한다.
- 원격 console/display socket은 서로 다른 BFF와 server-assigned topic ACL을 사용하고, display credential로 private topic 구독 시 403이 되는 통합 테스트를 필수로 한다.
- 내부 RAG는 retrieval 전 authorization, source materialization 시 재인가, publication 직전 revision/hash/ACL 재인가의 3중 TOCTOU gate를 사용한다. ANN 후 post-filter만 가능한 저장소는 수용하지 않는다.
- `presenter can read`와 `audience can see`는 별도 정책이며, 내부 제목·URI·ACL·raw excerpt는 명시적 declassification 없이는 공개 DTO에 포함하지 않는다.
- 오디오 권한과 데이터 처리 동의는 분리한다. app origin만 mic 권한을 가지며 원음은 메모리 내 최대 30초 retry buffer 외에는 저장하지 않고, transcript·embedding·report 삭제 cascade를 session 단위로 시험한다.
- 원격 WSS protocol은 revisioned authoritative snapshot, idempotent commandId, controllerEpoch, role-scoped snapshot, gap 시 full resync를 사용한다. offline 중 relative next/toggle은 자동 replay하지 않는다.
- pairing QR에 secret을 담을지, 인증된 device-authorization transaction만 담을지는 상충해 skeptic 반론으로 넘겼다.
- PWA 캐시는 shell, 현재 deck, 이미 승인된 evidence asset, 복구 안내만 versioned precache한다. 서버 불가/기기 offline/display disconnect를 구분하고 마지막 sync와 freshness를 표시한다.
- session credential은 Account/PresentationControl/Device/AudienceDisplay 네 종류의 opaque host-only cookie로 나누고, role 변경·handoff·종료 시 회전/폐기하며 WSS도 즉시 닫는다.
- 공개 이미지·인용은 RightsRecord가 없는 경우 default-deny한다. unknown license는 private link candidate로만 남기고, 승인된 asset hash만 자체 CDN에서 제공한다.
- public byte invariant를 확정했다: Audience의 HTTP/WSS/DOM/storage/cache/telemetry는 `PublishedAudienceCard`만의 함수여야 한다. audience service account는 별도 published store/topic만 읽는다.
- 미러 모드는 발표 PC에 AudienceDisplaySession만 두고 개인 기기에 Console을 두는 것을 기본 보안 모드로 권고한다. topology 변화 시 Console privacy curtain을 즉시 적용하고 재확인 전 비공개 이벤트 전달을 중지한다.

# 보고서 디자인 명세

## 형식

- 한국어 Markdown 원본과 독립 실행형 HTML 보고서를 함께 제공한다.
- 신청서의 공공기관 제안서 문맥을 따르되, 분석 보고서처럼 명료한 계층과 여백을 사용한다.
- HTML은 인쇄와 화면 읽기 모두에 적합해야 한다.

## 시각 언어

- 배경: `#F5F7FB`, 본문 표면: `#FFFFFF`, 진한 본문: `#182033`
- 주 강조: `#3157D5`, 보조 청록: `#0F8B8D`, 경고: `#B45309`, 위험: `#B42318`
- 글꼴: `"Pretendard", "Noto Sans KR", system-ui, sans-serif`
- 제목은 굵기 700, 본문은 400~500, 표·캡션은 12~14px를 사용한다.
- 카드와 표는 12px 반경, 1px 중성 테두리, 낮은 그림자로 구분한다.

## 정보 구조

1. 표지와 한 문장 결론
2. 신청서 요구 해석
3. 권고 아키텍처
4. 확장 디스플레이 흐름
5. 화면 복제/원격 콘솔 흐름
6. 실시간 AI·RAG 파이프라인
7. 보안·프라이버시
8. 기술 스택 비교와 단계별 권고
9. 위험·검증 계획
10. 출처와 방법론

## 그림 표준

- Mermaid/SVG는 원래 종횡비를 유지하고 `object-fit: contain` 방식으로 표시한다.
- 모든 그림은 제목, 범례 또는 캡션을 가진다.
- 색만으로 상태를 구분하지 않고 텍스트 라벨과 도형을 함께 사용한다.
- 긴 한국어 제목은 의미 단위 줄바꿈을 사용하고 한 글자 고아 줄을 허용하지 않는다.

## 접근성

- 본문 대비 4.5:1 이상, 큰 텍스트 3:1 이상을 목표로 한다.
- 표 헤더와 의미 구조를 HTML 요소로 표현한다.
- 링크 텍스트만 읽어도 목적을 이해할 수 있게 한다.
- 인쇄 시 배경과 테두리가 사라져도 정보 계층이 유지되어야 한다.

- 신청서는 상시 LLM이 아니라 확정 발화와 현재 `slide_id`가 결합된 이벤트 기반 호출을 명시한다.

- 카드에는 `STALE`, `SUPERSEDED` 수명 상태가 필요하고, 미검증 상태는 청중 화면으로 절대 전달하지 않는다.
- security-privacy는 단순 라우트 분리가 부족하다고 지적했다. 공개 화면은 별도 origin·topic·최소 DTO를 사용하고, 비공개 데이터를 DOM에 숨겨 전달하는 방식을 금지해야 한다.
- pwa-platform 반론 결과 UI 별도 origin은 BroadcastChannel, opener, service worker lifecycle을 깨뜨린다. 결론은 same-origin UI route + 역할별 서버 topic/DTO/권한이다.
- remote-console은 WSS relay를 기본으로 하고 ICE/TURN·signaling이 필요한 WebRTC는 선택적 fast path로 제한하라고 권고했다.
- 5초 목표는 공개 SLA가 아니라 Presenter Console의 최대 3개 추천 SLA로 해석되었다.
- origin 경계는 재논쟁 상태다. same-origin은 BroadcastChannel/SW 조정이 쉽지만, 보안팀은 쿠키·localStorage·공개 SW 격리를 위해 별도 origin을 요구한다. WSS relay를 기준 통신으로 삼으면 공개 창과 콘솔이 BroadcastChannel을 공유할 필요가 없으므로 별도 origin이 유력하다.
- stack-economics는 Vite+React PWA, Supabase(Postgres/pgvector/Auth/Realtime/Storage), Deepgram Nova-3, OpenAI API의 월 $0 MVP를 제안했다. 다만 가격·무료 한도는 시점 의존이며 한국어 STT 정확도와 Supabase 휴면 복구를 실측해야 한다.
- origin 논쟁은 보안 우선으로 수렴했다. `app.example`(setup/controller/presenter)와 `stage.example`(public display)를 분리하고 WSS만 data plane으로 사용한다.

- 내부 RAG principal은 인증 서버에서 도출하고 Postgres RLS로 default-deny한다. 검색 엔진의 문자열 필터만 authorization으로 취급하지 않는다.
- 원격 콘솔 QR에는 credential을 넣지 않는다. 128-bit pair_id, 90초 TTL, 양 기기 동일 확인 문자열, 기존 콘솔의 명시 승인, 단일 사용 후 새 presentation-scoped device session 발급 흐름을 사용한다.

- cross-origin launch 최종 흐름은 setup permission과 popup activation을 분리한다: 권한 확인 후 `Open audience display` 클릭으로 `noopener,noreferrer` stage를 배치하고, stage 자체 클릭으로 fullscreen한다. WSS presence가 liveness source다.
- Presentation API는 Cast/TV adapter 후보지만 attached Windows monitor의 deterministic geometry를 주지 못해 핵심 폴백에서 제외한다.
- 원격 console/display socket은 서로 다른 BFF와 server-assigned topic ACL을 사용하고, display credential로 private topic 구독 시 403이 되는 통합 테스트를 필수로 한다.
- 내부 RAG는 retrieval 전 authorization, source materialization 시 재인가, publication 직전 revision/hash/ACL 재인가의 3중 TOCTOU gate를 사용한다. ANN 후 post-filter만 가능한 저장소는 수용하지 않는다.

- 오디오 권한과 데이터 처리 동의는 분리한다. app origin만 mic 권한을 가지며 원음은 메모리 내 최대 30초 retry buffer 외에는 저장하지 않고, transcript·embedding·report 삭제 cascade를 session 단위로 시험한다.
- 원격 WSS protocol은 revisioned authoritative snapshot, idempotent commandId, controllerEpoch, role-scoped snapshot, gap 시 full resync를 사용한다. offline 중 relative next/toggle은 자동 replay하지 않는다.

- PWA 캐시는 shell, 현재 deck, 이미 승인된 evidence asset, 복구 안내만 versioned precache한다. 서버 불가/기기 offline/display disconnect를 구분하고 마지막 sync와 freshness를 표시한다.
- session credential은 Account/PresentationControl/Device/AudienceDisplay 네 종류의 opaque host-only cookie로 나누고, role 변경·handoff·종료 시 회전/폐기하며 WSS도 즉시 닫는다.
- 공개 이미지·인용은 RightsRecord가 없는 경우 default-deny한다. unknown license는 private link candidate로만 남기고, 승인된 asset hash만 자체 CDN에서 제공한다.

- remote-console은 WSS relay를 기본으로 하고 ICE/TURN·signaling이 필요한 WebRTC는 선택적 fast path로 제한하라고 권고했다.

- origin 경계는 재논쟁 상태다. same-origin은 BroadcastChannel/SW 조정이 쉽지만, 보안팀은 쿠키·localStorage·공개 SW 격리를 위해 별도 origin을 요구한다. WSS relay를 기준 통신으로 삼으면 공개 창과 콘솔이 BroadcastChannel을 공유할 필요가 없으므로 별도 origin이 유력하다.

- 브라우저 capability tier를 정의했다: Tier 0 수동 drag/fullscreen+WSS, Tier 1 Chromium desktop 자동 placement, Tier 2 설치형 standalone+offline shell. 설치는 멀티스크린 권한을 늘리지 않는다.

- Presentation API는 Cast/TV adapter 후보지만 attached Windows monitor의 deterministic geometry를 주지 못해 핵심 폴백에서 제외한다.
- 원격 console/display socket은 서로 다른 BFF와 server-assigned topic ACL을 사용하고, display credential로 private topic 구독 시 403이 되는 통합 테스트를 필수로 한다.

.omo/senpi-task/teams/runtime/d0d1b795-b762-40f8-8619-05bd591942e3/inboxes/lead/processed/529930c3-4861-44a5-9d9e-f41312948181.json:7:  "body": "ACCIDENTAL-LEAK LEAD: Formal invariant: every byte observable from Audience HTTP/WSS/DOM/storage/cache/telemetry must be a function ONLY of `PublishedAudienceCard`, never Candidate/Transcript/RAG/Console state. Enforce structurally: Audience service account can read only a separate `published_cards` store/topic; it has no credentials/network path to private DB/event bus. Publish writes an immutable schema (`additionalProperties:false`) of plain-text title/body, approved asset hash, public canonical citations/attribution, alt text, expiry. It rejects HTML/Markdown, unknown fields, internal URI/doc IDs, prompts/queries/transcript/speaker/team/ACL/provider/debug fields. Console sends only `candidate_id`; server builds DTO—client/model never submits audience JSON.

`SUPPORTED` is necessary, not sufficient: `publishable = evidence_supported AND source_current AND audience_classification=PUBLIC AND rights=publishable AND privacy_DLP=pass AND presenter_approval`. Default manual WYSIWYG audience preview. Internal-RAG-derived cards never auto-publish; for 5s auto mode, restrict to approved public corpus + no detected person/secret + deterministic template. DLP checks secrets, credentials, emails/phones/IDs, internal domains/IPs, classification labels and source ACL metadata; uncertainty fails private. Audience errors are generic, with correlation ID only—never stack/provider response/search query.

Display-mode fail-safe: before private snapshot delivery, show Public Test Pattern on Audience and Privacy Curtain on Console; presenter confirms physical placement, producing `topology_fingerprint + display_instance + verified_at`. Extended mode subscribes to `screenschange/currentscreenchange`; any screen removal/change or uncertainty immediately curtains Console and stops private events until re-confirmed. Window Management API is experimental/limited and cannot detect every OS mirroring/capture case, so this is risk reduction, not a guarantee. In mirrored mode, presentation PC gets ONLY AudienceDisplaySession and never logs into Console; private Console runs on paired personal device. Recommend this mode whenever confidentiality matters.

Operational leakage controls: persistent PUBLIC/PRIVATE color+watermark chrome; emergency privacy-curtain control; raw transcript/source collapsed and press-to-reveal; no team-message link previews; browser notifications/session replay/APM screenshots disabled; Windows Do Not Disturb preflight; share only Audience window, never desktop. Console: no-store, no sensitive SW/Cache API/IndexedDB/localStorage, Clear-Site-Data on end/logout, privacy curtain on pagehide; Audience origin disables microphone/camera/display-capture/notifications and loads only self-hosted scripts/assets. No app can prevent OS screenshots, HDMI mirroring, OBS or shoulder surfing—remote private device is the hard mitigation.

Leak tests: packet/DOM/storage inspection proves Audience never sees private fields; fuzz unknown/PII/internal fields rejects publication; reconnect snapshot is role-filtered; error injection remains generic; topology event curtains before next private render; mirror workflow has no Console cookie; expired card disappears; service worker offline serves no private snapshot; logs/APM contain IDs only.

Sources: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ScreenDetails ; https://www.w3.org/TR/window-management/ ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Permissions-Policy/display-capture ; https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Logging_Cheat_Sheet.html ; https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Error_Handling_Cheat_Sheet.html ; https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/HTML5_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html",

Prepare = session brief, content/evidence, team/roles, display/device setup, rehearsal/readiness. Live = Public Stage + Presenter Console + Team Signals as role-specific views of one session state. Review = timeline, evidence ledger, decisions, incidents, exports/share. Presenter desktop: persistent health/status bar; three regions Now (dominant), Next (preview), Signals (evidence requests, messages, faults); sticky transport controls remain spatially stable. Phone/second device: single-column Now with bottom tabs Now / Next / Signals and a thumb-reachable control dock; never squeeze desktop columns. Public stage: zero app nav/private chrome, only approved content, optional captions/session code, and explicit holding/reconnecting/end states. Evidence has two projections: public card = claim/source/date/status; operator card = plus excerpt, provenance URL, reviewer, confidence, publish/hold actions. Team messaging should be structured operational signals (Urgent cue, Evidence request, Review, Ops), with acknowledge/resolve/pin; general chat is secondary and must never overlay the public stage.",
.omo/senpi-task/teams/runtime/d0d1b795-b762-40f8-8619-05bd591942e3/inboxes/lead/processed/7aa947a1-ba63-4c43-94b1-24099b8b526e.json:7:  "body": "FINAL REALTIME-AI SYNTHESIS

Recommended MVP architecture: upload worker (python-pptx + LibreOffice-rendered PDF/PyMuPDF; OCR/VLM only on failed/visual slides) -> canonical deck/slide/version records + cached context -> authoritative browser viewer emits slide events -> WebSocket audio to Korean streaming STT -> final transcript + current slide -> deterministic trigger + small structured-output LLM -> parallel internal hybrid search and external web search -> origin fetch/anchor -> deterministic field checks + compact verifier -> verdict -> Presenter Console approval -> audience card. Persist all transitions as immutable session events; Redis Streams consumers are idempotent; post-report recomputes from events rather than aggregating UI values.

Five-second recommendation budget, measured from utterance boundary/finalization trigger to Presenter Console (NOT presenter approval): STT endpoint/final 0.35/0.70s p50/p95; fusion+trigger+query 0.15/0.35; parallel internal/external retrieval 0.35/0.80; parallel origin fetch+parse 0.50/1.20; deterministic checks+compact verifier 0.45/1.10; rank/persist/push/render 0.10/0.25 = 1.9s p50, 4.4s allocated p95, 0.6s headroom. This is an engineering target, not a vendor guarantee. Enforce 4.4s cutoff, max 2-3 origin fetches, cancellation, caching of canonical sources, and abstain on timeout. Use partial STT only to precompute embeddings/query candidates; never publish from it.

Stack comparison:
A) Lean/recommended: web viewer + single API/orchestrator, Azure Speech or Deepgram, Postgres+pgvector+FTS+RLS, Redis Streams, Brave/Tavily, object storage. Fewest services, DB-enforced ACL, easy event/report joins; tune selective ANN.
B) Azure integrated: Azure Speech + AI Search hybrid/prefilter + Service Bus + Blob/Container Apps/OpenAI. Managed, documented Korean support; more cost/lock-in, and security-filter principal is NOT authentication.
C) Self-hosted: faster-whisper/live wrapper + Postgres/Qdrant/OpenSearch + NATS/Redis + local LLM. Best data control, but GPU/ops burden and no cited proof of Korean streaming latency; post-MVP unless offline is mandatory.

Verification contract: structured model output may propose `{claim, query, expected_fields}`, never URLs/ACL/slide IDs/numbers as truth. Fetch source yourself. Record `source_url, canonical_url, retrieved_at, published/effective date, content_hash, anchor, exact quote/table cell`; normalize and compare number/unit/date/entity deterministically before semantic support classification. Structured Outputs guarantees schema, not factuality; OpenAI itself says models may hallucinate and errors are worse than abstention: https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/structured-outputs and https://openai.com/index/why-language-models-hallucinate/ .

ACL/security invariants: authenticated server derives principals; DB/search prefilter before similarity; verifier and publication recheck ACL+revision+hash; audience payload must omit internal document name/path/quote even when presenter can access it. Use default-deny RLS: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-rowsecurity.html . External fetcher needs SSRF controls (HTTP/S only, resolve/check every redirect, block private/link-local/metadata IPs, size/type/time caps, sandbox parsing): https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Server_Side_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html . Treat fetched pages/internal docs as untrusted data, never instructions.

Caveats / unverifiable from vendor docs: (1) <=5s p95 end-to-end; must load-test. (2) Korean WER/number/entity accuracy and Korean-English code-switch behavior; run a target-corpus bake-off across Azure/Google/AWS/Deepgram. (3) Search API result freshness/primary-source recall. (4) LLM support-verdict precision. (5) a 10-person user study is not enough to claim market differentiation/generalization. (6) 'all sources original' is infeasible for blocked/paywalled/dynamic pages; UI should report unavailable origin, not use snippet as evidence. (7) C-05 auto-publication is incompatible with applicant p10 approval promise.

Core citations already sent: applicant PDF pp2-11,15; python-pptx, PyMuPDF, LibreOffice, Reveal.js; Azure/Google/AWS/Deepgram STT; Redis/NATS; Brave/Tavily; Azure hybrid + security trimming; pgvector/Postgres RLS; OWASP excessive agency; Kim 2018 Korean articulation-rate study.",

.omo/senpi-task/teams/runtime/d0d1b795-b762-40f8-8619-05bd591942e3/inboxes/lead/processed/8d359d36-8761-4c9d-81b7-623db4ac68aa.json:7:  "body": "RAG/ACL LEAD: Authorization must wrap retrieval, not be delegated to vector search or the LLM. Server derives `AuthzContext(tenant, subject, groups, clearance, purpose, presentation, policy_version)` from the session; clients/model cannot supply it. Every chunk is immutable metadata + bytes: `tenant_id, doc_id, chunk_id, revision, content_hash, classification, allowed_subjects/groups, valid_from/to, license_id`. Hard tenant isolation uses a separate namespace/index (preferred) or an immutable tenant prefilter. Within tenant, ABAC/relationship filter MUST execute before ANN/top-k; then policy engine post-authorizes every returned object. A vector store that only post-filters top-k fails acceptance.

TOCTOU gates: authorize at query; reauthorize when source bytes are materialized; reauthorize current ACL + exact revision/content_hash immediately before card creation/publication. ACL/revision change invalidates vector chunks and all derived caches. Policy engine unavailable/stale/missing metadata => zero results, never service-account fallback. Cache key includes tenant + authorization fingerprint/policy version + corpus revision; raw internal results are never shared across principals, while only public corpus may use shared cache.

Critical distinction: `presenter can read` NEVER implies `audience can see`. Publication calls a separate `can_publish_to_audience` policy against source classification/license and the minimal card DTO. Internal document title, URI, ACL/group names, raw excerpt and anchor stay private unless explicitly declassified. Citations are deterministic retrieval-service handles resolved from stored source metadata/hash—not model-invented URLs.

Treat documents/web results as hostile prompt input. Retrieved text cannot alter tool policy, choose corpus/filter, invoke arbitrary URLs, or publish. LLM has read-only allowlisted tools and outputs an untrusted candidate; only deterministic verifier + publish policy transition changes state. Embeddings inherit document classification, encryption, tenant isolation, retention/deletion, and vendor no-training/no-retention rules.

Acceptance tests must prove: cross-tenant deny; unauthorized group deny; ACL revoked between retrieval/render deny; stale revision/hash deny; policy outage fail-closed; poisoned document cannot alter tools/publish; cache cannot replay another principal; internal-readable/public-not-approved card denied. OWASP says deny-by-default, validate authorization every request, and prefer attribute/relationship policy; OWASP also states RAG does not eliminate indirect prompt injection. Sources: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.html ; https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/LLM_Prompt_Injection_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html ; https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm01-prompt-injection/ ; https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm08-vector-and-embedding-weaknesses/ ; https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/162/upd2/final",
.omo/senpi-task/teams/runtime/d0d1b795-b762-40f8-8619-05bd591942e3/inboxes/lead/processed/9e8786bc-b57e-4403-bba9-934a11d68c03.json:7:  "body": "EXHAUSTIVE PWA/BROWSER CAPABILITY REPORT (official sources fetched in full; BCD current main branch checked 2026-08-13)

A. WINDOW MANAGEMENT / MULTI-DISPLAY
- API: `screen.isExtended` (multi-screen boolean, secure context, no permission prompt), `window.getScreenDetails()` (detailed screens; may prompt), `ScreenDetails.screens/currentScreen`, `screenschange`, `currentscreenchange`, per-screen `change`. Details include coordinates, work area, DPI, labels, primary/internal status. `getScreenDetails()` rejects `NotAllowedError` when Permissions Policy blocks `window-management` or user denies. Default Permissions-Policy allowlist is `self`; delegate iframe with `allow="window-management"`. Sources: W3C https://www.w3.org/TR/window-management/ ; MDN https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window_Management_API ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/getScreenDetails ; policy https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Permissions-Policy/window-management ; Chrome https://developer.chrome.com/docs/capabilities/web-apis/window-management
- Compatibility (MDN BCD): `getScreenDetails`, `screen.isExtended`, ScreenDetails landed Chrome 100 and Edge mirror; Firefox false; Safari false. Chrome Android reports API mirror for getScreenDetails/isExtended but ScreenDetails and events false; therefore product-grade target is Chromium desktop, not mobile. Permissions query descriptor `window-management` starts Chrome 111, false Firefox/Safari/Chrome Android. Raw BCD: https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/api/Window.json ; /Screen.json ; /ScreenDetails.json ; /Permissions.json
- Use feature detection (`'getScreenDetails' in window`), never UA detection. Handle denied permission and screen hot-plug/reconfiguration. Coordinates can be negative in virtual arrangements. `avail*` excludes OS UI and is the safer placement region.
- Exact product implication: extended mode is progressive enhancement. Chromium desktop can offer automatic stage placement; every other browser needs ordinary second-window/manual-drag or single-screen mode.

B. WINDOW.OPEN / POPUP RULES
- `window.open()` is broadly available, but browsers decide tab vs popup and may correct requested size/position to keep the whole popup inside an OS work area. It returns WindowProxy or `null` when popup blocked. New URL load is asynchronous; initial context is `about:blank`. Source: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/open
- Modern browsers require direct user input and a separate user gesture for each `window.open()` call. MDN Window Management usage explicitly recommends opening at most one new window at once, reusing named windows, and showing popup-blocker recovery instructions: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window_Management_API/Using
- Important narrow exception in Window Management spec: after a targeted fullscreen request, the spec permits one popup placement within the transient-activation interval, enabling fullscreen on one screen + one popup on another from one click. This does NOT license arbitrary fan-out. Source: https://www.w3.org/TR/window-management/
- Cross-origin stage placement works, but no DOM/function access. Restricted WindowProxy ordinarily retains close/closed/focus/blur/postMessage; COOP can sever it and make `closed === true`. Sources already sent in origin verdict.
- iOS BCD caveat: `window.open` partial; MDN BCD says it will not function if target is omitted or `_blank`, so use a stable named target if mobile fallback matters.

C. FULLSCREEN
- `Element.requestFullscreen()` requires transient user activation in the requesting document; it is also policy-controlled (`fullscreen`, default allowlist self). Users can always exit; support itself can be unavailable due to user preference, security risk, or platform limitation. Sources: WHATWG https://fullscreen.spec.whatwg.org/ ; MDN https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Fullscreen_API ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/requestFullscreen
- Window Management adds experimental `{screen: ScreenDetailed}` to target a display. Do not assume cross-browser support merely because `requestFullscreen()` supports an options object.
- Cross-origin implication: controller cannot invoke stage DOM fullscreen. WSS/postMessage does not transfer user activation. Cross-origin audience must expose its own local `Enter fullscreen` button/gesture. Sized placement is the fallback.
- Compatibility BCD for base requestFullscreen: modern Chrome 71+, Edge 79+, Firefox 64+, Safari 16.4+. iOS Safari 16.4 is iPad-only, not iPhone, shows a non-disableable overlay, and swipe-down exits; unsuitable as a guaranteed clean presentation surface. Raw: https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/api/Element.json
- Manifest `display: fullscreen` is separate from Fullscreen API; it controls installed-app launch display, can coexist with `document.fullscreenElement === null`, and falls back `fullscreen -> standalone -> minimal-ui -> browser`. Prefer `standalone` for control app, explicit Fullscreen API for stage. Source: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Progressive_web_apps/Manifest/Reference/display

D. PERMISSIONS MODEL
- Permissions API only reports aggregate state (`granted|denied|prompt`) across secure-context, Permissions Policy, interaction, and user choice. It does not itself grant and cannot revoke; `Permissions.revoke()` was removed. Listen to PermissionStatus `change`, and always still handle the actual API rejection. Sources: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Permissions_API ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Permissions/query ; spec https://www.w3.org/TR/permissions/
- Querying an unsupported descriptor rejects TypeError; catch it. Generic query support is Chrome 43+, Firefox 46+, Safari 16+, but individual descriptor support differs dramatically. `microphone` descriptor: Chrome 64+, Firefox 132+, Safari 16+. `window-management`: Chromium desktop only (Chrome 111+, Edge mirror). Raw BCD Permissions.json above.
- Permissions persist/revoke per browser policy and user settings; do not promise persistence. Query is status UX, actual invocation is authority.

E. MICROPHONE
- `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({audio:true})` is HTTPS/secure-context only; in insecure contexts `mediaDevices` is undefined. User permission is always required at least initially. Only top-level valid-origin documents may request unless top-level explicitly delegates `microphone` via Permissions Policy to iframe. Denial/policy/insecure failures commonly surface `NotAllowedError`; no matching device `NotFoundError`; unsatisfiable exact constraint `OverconstrainedError`; empty/all-false constraints TypeError; inactive document InvalidStateError. Source: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/getUserMedia ; spec https://w3c.github.io/mediacapture-main/

O-PWA-10 MDN/WebKit: install affordances differ sharply across Chromium desktop, Safari 17 Add to Dock, desktop Firefox, Android, and iOS 16.4+. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Progressive_web_apps/Guides/Making_PWAs_installable ; https://webkit.org/blog/14445/webkit-features-in-safari-17-0/ ; https://webkit.org/blog/13966/webkit-features-in-safari-16-4/

EXPANSION LEADS CLOSED
- Separate-origin conflict: closed with security-first split-origin verdict and explicit COOP tradeoff.
- Targeted fullscreen compatibility: closed as experimental/Chromium enhancement; local gesture mandatory.
- Service-worker-as-install-requirement: closed/refuted as universal claim; current Chrome and Edge can install without one.
- Installability-vs-capabilities coupling: closed/refuted; installation grants none of Window Management/mic/fullscreen powers.
- Cross-browser custom install prompt: closed/refuted; Chromium-only.
- Mobile multi-screen: closed as non-product-grade due interface/event BCD gaps.
- Cross-origin audience remote fullscreen: closed/refuted; user activation does not cross WSS/opener boundary.

No material open lead remains in the assigned axes. A hardware/browser manual test matrix would validate vendor behavior but would not change the standards-based architecture verdict.

## EXPAND",

.omo/senpi-task/teams/runtime/d0d1b795-b762-40f8-8619-05bd591942e3/inboxes/lead/processed/0e45fdc8-0476-4710-968c-0c216dee12a1.json:7:  "body": "REMOTE-CONSOLE DESIGN — origin and data-plane boundary

Recommendation: deploy two actual web origins, not only two routes:
- https://display.example.com — public presentation runtime; host-only Secure HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie; can receive public state and send only display receipts/health.
- https://console.example.com — Presenter Console; separate host-only cookie; can receive private state and issue typed commands.
- Each origin exposes its own same-origin `/api/*` and `/socket` BFF/proxy into an internal session service. Never set `Domain=.example.com`; never place bearer tokens in WebSocket query strings. Exact Origin allowlisting occurs at both edge and WebSocket upgrade. This is practical behind one CDN/load balancer and creates meaningful cookie, service-worker, DOM, CSP and BroadcastChannel boundaries. A distinct hostname alone is insufficient if parent-domain cookies or a shared overly broad backend ACL remain.

Server-side topic ACL (no client-side filtering):
1. `s/{sid}/public.state` — publisher: session service only; subscribers: display + presenter. Contract contains only `{slideId, buildStep, blackout, publicMedia, themeRevision}`.
2. `s/{sid}/presenter.private` — publisher: session service only; subscriber: presenter only. `{speakerNotes, nextSlidePreview, privateTimer, backstageMessages}`. It is never serialized for a display connection.
3. `s/{sid}/control.commands` — publisher: active presenter lease only; consumer: session service only. Typed allowlist such as `slide.set`, `slide.next`, `build.next`, `blackout.set`, `timer.start`; never arbitrary topic names or JSON patches.
4. `s/{sid}/control.receipts` — publisher: service/display; subscriber: presenter. Accepted/rejected/applied receipts, no notes.
5. `s/{sid}/display.receipts` — publisher: display only; service consumes; fields only `{commandId, revision, renderMs, result}`.
6. `s/{sid}/presenter.presence` — service to presenter only; device/lease diagnostics. Display gets, at most, one public boolean `controllerConnected` if product wants it.

Authorization tuple on every inbound frame: `{tenantId, sessionId, role, connectionId, controllerEpoch}` derived from the authenticated socket, never trusted from JSON. Broker subscriptions are materialized server-side from role; clients cannot SUBSCRIBE to arbitrary strings. The audience/display application has no code path or schema for `presenter.private`. Add a contract/integration assertion: authenticating as DISPLAY and requesting private topic returns `403 topic_forbidden`, and a complete display socket capture contains no private-schema field names or values.

Separate-origin trade-off: costs another deployment/CORS/BFF configuration and prevents BroadcastChannel across console/display by design; benefits are decisive because an XSS/service-worker compromise in public display origin cannot read presenter cookies/storage or join presenter BroadcastChannels. RFC 6454 defines origins and the Origin header: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6454 . Current cookie draft specifies the `__Host-` prefix as Secure, Path=/, no Domain: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-httpbis-rfc6265bis . WHATWG says BroadcastChannel is for browsing contexts of a given origin, not devices: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/dev/web-messaging.html#broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts .

## EXPAND
- LEAD: If fully offline operation is mandatory, investigate managed local relay certificate provisioning; automatic fallback to cleartext LAN WebSocket is not acceptable.
- LEAD: Decide whether anonymous pairing is allowed; if yes, display-local approval/SAS is a security requirement because a public QR is observable by the audience.",
.omo/senpi-task/teams/runtime/d0d1b795-b762-40f8-8619-05bd591942e3/inboxes/lead/processed/1e1edb58-3c8d-4764-bbd1-ca051cf10666.json:7:  "body": "PAIRING LEAD: Treat phone/tablet pairing as a device-authorization transaction, never as sharing the presenter session. Existing authenticated console creates 128-bit CSPRNG pair_id, single-use, 90s TTL; QR appears ONLY on private console and contains no access/refresh token. New device must authenticate, scan/enter code, then both devices display the same short-authentication string and the existing console explicitly approves device name + requested scopes. Rate-limit code attempts per transaction/IP/account and kill after 5 failures; responses must not reveal valid/invalid session membership. Approval atomically consumes pair_id and creates a NEW opaque, server-side, presentation-scoped device session in __Host- Secure HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie. Default scopes console:read + card:publish only if explicitly requested; never tenant/admin/corpus privileges. Rotate on approval/role change; revoke on session end, unpair, logout, expiry; list active devices with revoke control. WebSocket topics are assigned server-side from the device principal; no arbitrary room IDs. Reauthorize every command and periodically revalidate long-lived connections. Never put credentials in URL/query/log/localStorage; never use a QR bearer token. RFC 8628 specifically requires high-entropy device codes, short expiry, rate limiting, polling limits, and user-code confirmation; RFC 9700 requires audience restriction and replay defenses. Sources: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8628.html ; https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9700.html ; https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Session_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html ; https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/WebSocket_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html",
.omo/senpi-task/teams/runtime/d0d1b795-b762-40f8-8619-05bd591942e3/inboxes/lead/processed/35465765-5969-4cd9-8ee9-bc54a03f41b3.json:7:  "body": "DEFENSE: separate origins do NOT block placement; they block DOM control, which we should deliberately replace with server lifecycle.

Exact launch flow: (1) Setup step A asks `console.example` for `getScreenDetails()` / `window-management` permission. (2) After permission resolves, require a second explicit `Open audience display` click so popup transient activation is fresh. In that click call `window.open('https://audience.example/display/<non-secret launch_id>', '_blank', 'popup,noopener,noreferrer,left=<screen.availLeft>,top=<screen.availTop>,width=<screen.availWidth>,height=<screen.availHeight>')`. Cross-origin navigation does not prevent `window.open` from selecting coordinates. Browsers may clamp/block it, and Window Management is limited/experimental, so manual drag-to-projector is mandatory fallback. (3) Audience connects to SAME-ORIGIN `wss://audience.example/ws` (reverse-proxied backend), consumes only public DTOs, and reports `ready/heartbeat/disconnected` through backend. Console uses `wss://console.example/ws`; server mediates commands/state with role auth. No BroadcastChannel/postMessage/client peer channel. (4) Fullscreen cannot be invoked by console on a cross-origin child. The target audience document needs its own click (`Enter fullscreen`) and calls `document.documentElement.requestFullscreen()`; because popup is already on target screen, default current screen suffices. `requestFullscreen({screen})` is experimental and still needs user activation, so do not make it a dependency. (5) Console observes display connection/size/fullscreen via WSS. Authorized `display.close` makes script-opened audience call `window.close()` itself; focus/close are best effort and never security controls.

Opener/COOP tradeoff: recommended `COOP: same-origin` on BOTH origins plus `noopener,noreferrer`; accept that console gets no usable WindowProxy (`closed/focus/close` unavailable) and use WSS health instead. This removes reverse-tabnabbing/opener navigation and prevents an audience XSS from reaching the console WindowProxy. The weaker alternative—console `COOP: same-origin-allow-popups`, audience `unsafe-none`, retain WindowProxy for `.closed/.close/.focus`—preserves convenience but creates a cross-origin opener bridge and is not worth it. Do not send a bearer token in launch URL: launch_id only correlates a provisional public display; if audience content is access-controlled, complete a separate one-use display pairing and issue an HttpOnly display cookie before content.

Topology safety: subscribe to `screenschange`/`currentscreenchange`; any removal, current-screen change, or mirror/extend uncertainty triggers `DISPLAY NEEDS CONFIRMATION`, never moves private state into audience. Audience remains public-only; console hides private panes behind a privacy curtain until re-confirmed.

Sources: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window_Management_API ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/open ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/requestFullscreen ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy ; https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/WebSocket_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Broadcast_Channel_API",
.omo/senpi-task/teams/runtime/d0d1b795-b762-40f8-8619-05bd591942e3/inboxes/lead/processed/3ce8a4f0-eb04-4260-8460-7d1339d72eb9.json:7:  "body": "CONCRETE PAIRING + WIRE PROTOCOL (JSON examples; schema-validated, `v` is protocol version)

Pair creation (display, authenticated presentation owner or one-time display bootstrap):
`POST https://display.example.com/api/sessions/{sid}/pairings`
request `{ "consoleKeyJkt":"<base64url SHA-256 JWK thumbprint>" }`
response `{ "pairingId":"p_...", "pairSecret":"<256-bit random base64url>", "expiresAt":"...", "qrUrl":"https://console.example.com/pair#p=p_...&s=<secret>" }`
Secret is in fragment so it is not part of the HTTP request URI; console JS reads it, immediately `history.replaceState(null,"","/pair")`, and never sends it to analytics/logging. Pairing DB stores `HMAC(serverPepper, secret)`, expiry <=120 s, state `ISSUED`; consume once atomically. Display shows QR plus four-word/SAS confirmation derived from the pairing transcript. If presenter is already account-authenticated, server must verify authorization to control the underlying deck/session; otherwise require explicit display-local approve/SAS before elevation.

Redeem (console):
`POST https://console.example.com/api/pairings/p_.../redeem`
`{ "pairSecret":"...", "consoleKeyJwk":{...}, "sas":"optional-display-confirmed-code" }`
response via Set-Cookie, not JSON bearer token: host-only `__Host-presenter=<opaque session>; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/`; body `{ "sessionId":"s_...", "role":"PRESENTER", "controllerEpoch":7, "socketUrl":"wss://console.example.com/socket" }`. Server binds redeem to the key thumbprint committed at creation (or commits it atomically on first redeem); rate-limit pairingId/IP/account and return generic failure.

Display socket hello:
`{"v":1,"type":"hello","connectionId":"c_d","role":"DISPLAY","sessionId":"s_","lastSeenRevision":41,"capabilities":["public-state-v1"]}`
Server welcome:
`{"v":1,"type":"welcome","connectionId":"c_d","heartbeatMs":15000,"serverTime":"...","controllerEpoch":7,"currentRevision":44}`
Authoritative public snapshot (always after first connect; after reconnect when gap not replayable):
`{"v":1,"type":"public.snapshot","revision":44,"state":{"slideId":"slide-8","buildStep":2,"blackout":false,"publicMedia":null,"themeRevision":3}}`
Presenter receives a distinct `presenter.snapshot` carrying `{publicState, privateState, controllerEpoch}` only on console origin/socket.

Presenter command:
`{"v":1,"type":"command","commandId":"01J...","controllerEpoch":7,"baseRevision":44,"name":"slide.next","args":{}}`
Server accepted (only after auth, active lease, epoch and revision checks):
`{"v":1,"type":"command.accepted","commandId":"01J...","revision":45}`
Public event to display/presenter:
`{"v":1,"type":"public.state","revision":45,"causationId":"01J...","patch":{"slideId":"slide-9","buildStep":0}}`
Display applied receipt:
`{"v":1,"type":"display.applied","commandId":"01J...","revision":45,"renderMs":11,"result":"OK"}`
Server forwards sanitized console receipt:
`{"v":1,"type":"command.applied","commandId":"01J...","revision":45,"displayId":"primary","renderMs":11}`
Reject example:
`{"v":1,"type":"error","requestId":"01J...","code":"STALE_REVISION","currentRevision":47,"retryable":true}`; console requests snapshot before retrying intent. Duplicate `commandId` under the same session returns the original result and never reapplies.

Heartbeat/reconnect:
- Use protocol ping/pong at infrastructure layer when server library exposes it; browser JS cannot originate protocol Ping, so also send application `{"v":1,"type":"ping","nonce":"..."}` / `pong` if end-to-end UI liveness is required.
- Mark degraded after 2 missed 15 s heartbeats; reconnect exponential full jitter 250 ms -> 500 ms -> 1 s -> 2 s -> cap 5 s. Visibility/network-online may trigger an immediate attempt, never a reconnect storm.
- On reconnect, authenticate fresh host cookie and send `resume {lastSeenRevision,lastAckedCommandId,controllerEpoch}`. Server replies either ordered `events {fromRevision,toRevision,items}` if contiguous journal retained, or a full role-scoped snapshot. Client applies only `revision == local+1`; duplicate revisions ignored; gaps trigger snapshot. Commands created while disconnected stay visibly pending and are NOT blindly replayed: only idempotent absolute intents (`slide.set`, `blackout.set`) may be retried with same commandId/baseRevision after snapshot; relative `next/previous/toggle` require user confirmation or conversion to absolute desired state.
- Presenter lease: single active controller with monotonically increasing `controllerEpoch`. Takeover increments epoch; every old queued frame becomes `STALE_CONTROLLER`. Display never accepts direct peer commands as authority: optional WebRTC fast-path frames still carry server-issued epoch/authorization and are reconciled through cloud state, otherwise a stolen LAN peer can bypass ACL.

WebSocket RFC specifies bidirectional framing, Ping/Pong and closing: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455 . RFC 3986 fragment semantics: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986#section-3.5 . RFC 8628 is a useful precedent for short-lived codes, brute-force rate limiting and non-textual complete URIs, but this custom presentation pairing is not OAuth device grant: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8628 .

## EXPAND
- LEAD: Product must choose takeover UX: deny second console, approval on current console/display, or authenticated owner force-takeover. Epoch mechanism supports all three.
- DEAD END: WebSocket subprotocol Ping is unavailable to browser JS; application ping is needed for UI-level liveness despite intermediary protocol Ping/Pong.",
.omo/senpi-task/teams/runtime/d0d1b795-b762-40f8-8619-05bd591942e3/inboxes/lead/processed/4e3d3441-358e-4aed-a59c-18e51e7646e5.json:7:  "body": "SESSION-HIJACK LEAD: Use four server-side opaque session classes, never one JWT reused everywhere: AccountSession; short-lived PresentationControlSession; paired DeviceSession; AudienceDisplaySession (`audience:read` only). Each has independent 128-bit CSPRNG ID, revocation and cookie on its own origin: `__Host-<name>=...; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/` (no Domain). Rotate on authentication, presentation start, pairing/role/control handoff; invalidate old ID and force old WSS closed. End/logout/revoke closes every socket immediately through revocation pubsub. Recommended bounds: 30m idle, 8h absolute, and hard expiration at presentation end + short cleanup grace. Never URL/query/fragment/localStorage/IndexedDB/log tokens.

Make WSS same-origin via reverse proxy (`console.example/ws`, `audience.example/ws`). Exact `Origin` allowlist at handshake (full string, not suffix); authenticate cookie before 101; derive subscriptions server-side—client never supplies arbitrary tenant/room/topic. Validate JSON schema/size/type, rate limit, authorize EVERY message, periodically revalidate long connections and close at auth/ACL expiry. Audience principal has no command types. Reconnect returns a role-filtered current snapshot, never raw event backlog. Do not put auth in WebSocket query strings.

Prevent CSRF/CSWSH: SameSite is defense-in-depth, plus synchronizer token on every state-changing HTTP request, exact Origin/Referer policy, Fetch Metadata reject `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`, and no GET mutations. Prevent XSS/token riding: render STT/RAG/model/search as text (no model HTML), contextual output encoding/sanitization, strict nonce CSP + Trusted Types, no third-party JS, `object-src/base-uri/frame-ancestors 'none'`. Hijack/race control: exactly one primary controller lease. Every mutating command carries server-issued `controller_epoch`, monotonic `command_seq`, idempotency UUID and candidate/card ID (never arbitrary audience JSON). Handoff explicitly increments epoch and invalidates old controller; stale/out-of-order/duplicate commands reject. Pair/start/end/handoff are security audit events. Do not hard-bind IP (breaks mobile); instead show active device/last-seen, alert on concurrent/geographic anomalies, provide revoke-all.

Acceptance: malicious Origin socket rejected; expired/rotated cookie cannot reconnect; audience `publish` denied; arbitrary topic denied; old controller after handoff denied; duplicate/out-of-order command denied; cross-site POST denied; session end closes all sockets; XSS corpus payload is inert; private SW/cache/log/history contain no credential/content.

Why this materially matters:
1) `app.example.com` and `present.example.com` are different origins because origin is scheme/host/port; subdomains do not qualify as same-origin. MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Same-origin_policy
2) A cross-origin `window.opener` is only a restricted WindowProxy. You cannot read variables/functions/DOM; only a limited allowlist such as `postMessage`, `close`, `focus`, `blur`, `closed`, and limited navigation remains. All other property access throws SecurityError. MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/opener
3) Cross-origin windows can synchronize with `window.postMessage`, but every send must use an exact `targetOrigin`, and every receiver must validate `event.origin` (and ideally `event.source`). This is viable but adds a security-critical protocol and loses direct shared state/DOM access. MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/postMessage
4) `BroadcastChannel` works only among same-origin contexts in the same storage partition. Separate subdomains cannot share a channel. MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Broadcast_Channel_API
5) Service workers are origin-bound: registration rejects unless `scriptURL` and scope are same-origin with the registering page. Separate UI subdomains therefore require independent registrations/caches/update lifecycles. MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ServiceWorkerContainer/register
6) COOP can sever opener even for otherwise expected relationships. `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` isolates browsing context groups and prevents a cross-origin opener reference; if cross-origin UI is unavoidable, ensure header strategy does not accidentally null/sever the channel, or use an explicit server relay/WebSocket. MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy
7) `document.domain` relaxation is deprecated and has limitations; do not use it as an architecture escape hatch. Same-origin policy source above.

Architecture boundary: SAME ORIGIN `/control`, `/presenter`, `/stage`, `/assets`, `/sw.js`; use BroadcastChannel as the resilient fan-out bus and optionally retain direct Window refs only for lifecycle/focus/close. SEPARATE ORIGIN only for API calls that do not need browser-window coordination (e.g. `api.example.com`), with CORS/auth or reverse-proxy it behind `/api`. If sensitive admin is hosted separately, communicate server-side rather than joining the presentation window mesh. This preserves Window Management placement (which itself can open any URL) while avoiding avoidable opener/channel/SW fragmentation.",

Assets/invariants: speaker notes/next preview/backstage messages remain presenter-only; only current controller changes authoritative public state; command ordering is deterministic; pairing grants expire and are single-use; session/account isolation; service availability. Trust boundaries: public display DOM/origin, private console origin, QR optical channel, browser-to-edge TLS, internal relay/broker, optional LAN peer path. Attackers: audience member with camera/QR visibility, malicious website in either browser, LAN peer, compromised display-origin JS/XSS/service worker, stolen/replayed URL/token, stale former controller, malicious tenant, network observer, overloaded client/server.

Attack -> defense -> verification evidence:
1. Audience photographs QR and races presenter. Defense: 256-bit fragment secret, <=120 s, atomic one-use redemption, authenticated account/deck authorization; for anonymous mode require display-local approval or compare a 4-word SAS on both devices. Short human codes alone need strict rate limiting; RFC 8628 section 5 covers brute force, remote phishing and session spying: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8628 . Test two simultaneous redeems: exactly one succeeds; unauthorized account cannot control deck.
2. Pair secret leaks through URL logs/referrer/history/analytics. Defense: fragment, immediate URL scrub, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, no third-party scripts on pair page, redact pairing/token fields from telemetry, CSP; secret hash/HMAC at rest. RFC 3986 says fragment is separated before dereference: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986#section-3.5 . Test proxy/access logs contain pairingId but never secret.
3. Cross-site WebSocket hijacking/CSRF. Browser automatically attaches cookies. Defense: Secure HttpOnly SameSite=Strict host-only cookie; exact `Origin` allowlist during upgrade, Fetch Metadata where available, CSRF token for pairing mutation endpoints, reject `Origin:null`; authenticate and authorize every connection/message. RFC 6455 explicitly includes Origin for protection against unauthorized cross-origin use: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-10.2 . Test evil origin upgrade gets 403 despite valid cookie.
4. XSS/service worker on public display steals private state. Defense: separate `display.example.com` and `console.example.com`, no parent-domain cookie, distinct CSP/build/deploy/service workers; broker materializes role subscriptions and never serializes private payload to display. Origin boundary evidence RFC 6454: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6454 ; `__Host-` cookie draft: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-httpbis-rfc6265bis#section-4.1.3.2 . Canary test: seed unique secret note, capture every display HTTP/WS/RTC byte, assert canary absent; DISPLAY subscribe to private topic returns `TOPIC_FORBIDDEN`.
5. Client changes `role`, `sessionId`, topic, or tenant in JSON. Defense: derive auth tuple from socket session; typed inbound union; server constructs subscriptions; per-frame tenant/session/role/epoch ACL; no wildcard broker subjects. Fuzz test fields/topic names never expand privileges.
6. Replay/duplicate/out-of-order command changes slide twice. Defense: unique commandId idempotency table, baseRevision compare-and-set, monotonic revision, active controllerEpoch, absolute commands preferred. Test duplicate/reordered frames and reconnect replay yield one state transition.
7. Former/lost console keeps control after takeover. Defense: increment controllerEpoch transactionally, revoke prior lease/socket/session, reject all old frames, short session TTL and explicit end-presentation revoke. Test queued old command after takeover returns STALE_CONTROLLER.
8. WebRTC signaling MITM or peer substitution. DTLS encrypts channel but peer identity depends on authenticated fingerprint signaling; RFC 8827 explains fingerprints and signaling trust: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8827#section-4 . Defense: exchange offers/answers/ICE only over authenticated WSS within paired session; bind DTLS fingerprint to connection/role/epoch; do not authorize based on data-channel possession. Test modified fingerprint/signaling fails or produces a channel with no control authorization.
9. ICE candidate privacy and LAN exposure. Host/server-reflexive candidates reveal network information; TURN adds relay and credentials. Defense: optional WebRTC only after pairing/consent; `iceTransportPolicy:"relay"` for privacy-sensitive cloud mode or accept direct candidate exposure explicitly; ephemeral TURN credentials scoped to session/TTL; never expose private topics on RTC. RFC 8445: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8445 ; TURN authentication RFC 8656 section 3.2: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8656#section-3.2 .
10. UDP blocked or restrictive symmetric NAT makes P2P/WebTransport fail. Defense: WSS/TCP 443 remains canonical; WebRTC has TURN fallback but still needs operated relay; WebTransport must fall back because RFC 9114 says blocking UDP can prevent QUIC and clients should use TCP HTTP: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9114#section-3.1 . Chaos test blocks UDP and verifies control remains on WSS.
11. Oversized/high-rate frames or slow display causes memory/CPU exhaustion. Browser WebSocket API has no standardized inbound backpressure guarantee adequate for unbounded data; defense max 16 KiB control frames, schema depth/string bounds, per-role rates, bounded outbound queue, coalesce superseded public state, close 1009 for too large / 1008 policy violation, avoid sending slide assets over control channel. Load test slow consumer never grows queue without bound.
12. Notes leak via logs/errors/receipts/telemetry. Defense: explicit allowlisted DTO projection at producer (not redact later), separate sinks/access controls, never echo input on errors, data classification tests. Canary log scan and display-byte capture.
13. Broker/server operator sees private content. TLS/WSS is hop-to-server, not end-to-end against service. If operator-confidential notes are required, add application-layer E2EE with keys transferred via pairing and ciphertext-only broker; this complicates multi-console recovery/search. Do not imply WebRTC automatically solves it when signaling identity is server-controlled.
14. Downgrade to ws:// or insecure local relay. Defense: HTTPS/WSS only, HSTS, secure contexts, no automatic insecure LAN fallback. Fully offline mode requires provisioned trusted local certificate/relay.
15. Availability: QR guessing, connect storms, TURN exhaustion, reconnect herd. Defense: per-IP/account/pairing limits, quotas, full-jitter reconnect, bounded presence retention, ephemeral TURN credentials/bandwidth caps, observability alerts. Security controls must not put private payload values in metrics.

Attack/defense conclusion: separate origins are practical and worth the modest deployment cost, but are defense-in-depth; decisive confidentiality control is server-side role-specific serialization and broker ACL. The single strongest regression evidence is an end-to-end DISPLAY-role byte-capture canary proving a unique private note never crosses any display transport.

- DEAD END: Separate origins alone do not prevent backend/broker ACL mistakes or parent-domain cookie leakage; retain canary capture and host-only cookies.",

Network Working Group                                     T. Berners-Lee

Category: Standards Track                                  Adobe Systems
January 2005

Status of This Memo

This document specifies an Internet standards track protocol for the
Internet community, and requests discussion and suggestions for
improvements.  Please refer to the current edition of the "Internet
Official Protocol Standards" (STD 1) for the standardization state
and status of this protocol.  Distribution of this memo is unlimited.

Copyright Notice

Copyright (C) The Internet Society (2005).

Abstract

A Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) is a compact sequence of
characters that identifies an abstract or physical resource.  This
specification defines the generic URI syntax and a process for
resolving URI references that might be in relative form, along with
guidelines and security considerations for the use of URIs on the
Internet.  The URI syntax defines a grammar that is a superset of all
valid URIs, allowing an implementation to parse the common components
of a URI reference without knowing the scheme-specific requirements
of every possible identifier.  This specification does not define a
generative grammar for URIs; that task is performed by the individual
specifications of each URI scheme.

## [1](#section-1).  Introduction

A Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) provides a simple and extensible
means for identifying a resource.  This specification of URI syntax
and semantics is derived from concepts introduced by the World Wide
Web global information initiative, whose use of these identifiers
dates from 1990 and is described in "Universal Resource Identifiers
in WWW" \[[RFC1630](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1630)\].  The syntax is designed to meet the
recommendations laid out in "Functional Recommendations for Internet
Resource Locators" \[[RFC1736](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1736)\] and "Functional Requirements for Uniform
Resource Names" \[[RFC1737](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1737)\].

This document obsoletes \[[RFC2396](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2396)\], which merged "Uniform Resource
Locators" \[[RFC1738](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1738)\] and "Relative Uniform Resource Locators"
\[[RFC1808](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1808)\] in order to define a single, generic syntax for all URIs.
It obsoletes \[[RFC2732](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2732)\], which introduced syntax for an IPv6 address.
It excludes portions of [RFC 1738](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1738) that defined the specific syntax of
individual URI schemes; those portions will be updated as separate
documents.  The process for registration of new URI schemes is
defined separately by \[[BCP35](#ref-BCP35)\].  Advice for designers of new URI
schemes can be found in \[[RFC2718](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2718)\].  All significant changes from [RFC](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2396)
[2396](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2396) are noted in [Appendix D](#appendix-D).

This specification uses the terms "character" and "coded character
set" in accordance with the definitions provided in \[[BCP19](#ref-BCP19)\], and
"character encoding" in place of what \[[BCP19](#ref-BCP19)\] refers to as a
"charset".

### [1.1](#section-1.1).  Overview of URIs

URIs are characterized as follows:

Uniform

Uniformity provides several benefits.  It allows different types
of resource identifiers to be used in the same context, even when
the mechanisms used to access those resources may differ.  It
allows uniform semantic interpretation of common syntactic
conventions across different types of resource identifiers.  It
allows introduction of new types of resource identifiers without
interfering with the way that existing identifiers are used.  It
allows the identifiers to be reused in many different contexts,
thus permitting new applications or protocols to leverage a pre-
existing, large, and widely used set of resource identifiers.

Berners-Lee, et al.         Standards Track                     \[Page 4\]

---

[RFC 3986](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986)                   URI Generic Syntax               January 2005

Resource

This specification does not limit the scope of what might be a
resource; rather, the term "resource" is used in a general sense
for whatever might be identified by a URI.  Familiar examples
include an electronic document, an image, a source of information
with a consistent purpose (e.g., "today's weather report for Los
Angeles"), a service (e.g., an HTTP-to-SMS gateway), and a
collection of other resources.  A resource is not necessarily
accessible via the Internet; e.g., human beings, corporations, and
bound books in a library can also be resources.  Likewise,
abstract concepts can be resources, such as the operators and
operands of a mathematical equation, the types of a relationship
(e.g., "parent" or "employee"), or numeric values (e.g., zero,
one, and infinity).

Identifier

An identifier embodies the information required to distinguish
what is being identified from all other things within its scope of
identification.  Our use of the terms "identify" and "identifying"
refer to this purpose of distinguishing one resource from all
other resources, regardless of how that purpose is accomplished
(e.g., by name, address, or context).  These terms should not be
mistaken as an assumption that an identifier defines or embodies
the identity of what is referenced, though that may be the case
for some identifiers.  Nor should it be assumed that a system
using URIs will access the resource identified: in many cases,
URIs are used to denote resources without any intention that they
be accessed.  Likewise, the "one" resource identified might not be
singular in nature (e.g., a resource might be a named set or a
mapping that varies over time).

A URI is an identifier consisting of a sequence of characters
matching the syntax rule named <URI> in [Section 3](#section-3).  It enables
uniform identification of resources via a separately defined
extensible set of naming schemes ([Section 3.1](#section-3.1)).  How that
identification is accomplished, assigned, or enabled is delegated to
each scheme specification.

This specification does not place any limits on the nature of a
resource, the reasons why an application might seek to refer to a
resource, or the kinds of systems that might use URIs for the sake of
identifying resources.  This specification does not require that a
URI persists in identifying the same resource over time, though that
is a common goal of all URI schemes.  Nevertheless, nothing in this

Berners-Lee, et al.         Standards Track                     \[Page 5\]

---

[RFC 3986](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986)                   URI Generic Syntax               January 2005

specification prevents an application from limiting itself to
particular types of resources, or to a subset of URIs that maintains
characteristics desired by that application.

URIs have a global scope and are interpreted consistently regardless
of context, though the result of that interpretation may be in
relation to the end-user's context.  For example, "http://localhost/"
has the same interpretation for every user of that reference, even
though the network interface corresponding to "localhost" may be
different for each end-user: interpretation is independent of access.
However, an action made on the basis of that reference will take
place in relation to the end-user's context, which implies that an
action intended to refer to a globally unique thing must use a URI
that distinguishes that resource from all other things.  URIs that
identify in relation to the end-user's local context should only be
used when the context itself is a defining aspect of the resource,
such as when an on-line help manual refers to a file on the end-
user's file system (e.g., "file:///etc/hosts").

#### [1.1.1](#section-1.1.1).  Generic Syntax

Each URI begins with a scheme name, as defined in [Section 3.1](#section-3.1), that
refers to a specification for assigning identifiers within that
scheme.  As such, the URI syntax is a federated and extensible naming
system wherein each scheme's specification may further restrict the
syntax and semantics of identifiers using that scheme.

This specification defines those elements of the URI syntax that are
required of all URI schemes or are common to many URI schemes.  It
thus defines the syntax and semantics needed to implement a scheme-
independent parsing mechanism for URI references, by which the
scheme-dependent handling of a URI can be postponed until the
scheme-dependent semantics are needed.  Likewise, protocols and data
formats that make use of URI references can refer to this
specification as a definition for the range of syntax allowed for all
URIs, including those schemes that have yet to be defined.  This
decouples the evolution of identification schemes from the evolution
of protocols, data formats, and implementations that make use of
URIs.

A parser of the generic URI syntax can parse any URI reference into
its major components.  Once the scheme is determined, further
scheme-specific parsing can be performed on the components.  In other
words, the URI generic syntax is a superset of the syntax of all URI
schemes.

#### [1.1.3](#section-1.1.3).  URI, URL, and URN

A URI can be further classified as a locator, a name, or both.  The
term "Uniform Resource Locator" (URL) refers to the subset of URIs
that, in addition to identifying a resource, provide a means of
locating the resource by describing its primary access mechanism
(e.g., its network "location").  The term "Uniform Resource Name"
(URN) has been used historically to refer to both URIs under the
"urn" scheme \[[RFC2141](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2141)\], which are required to remain globally unique
and persistent even when the resource ceases to exist or becomes
unavailable, and to any other URI with the properties of a name.

An individual scheme does not have to be classified as being just one
of "name" or "locator".  Instances of URIs from any given scheme may
have the characteristics of names or locators or both, often
depending on the persistence and care in the assignment of
identifiers by the naming authority, rather than on any quality of
the scheme.  Future specifications and related documentation should
use the general term "URI" rather than the more restrictive terms
"URL" and "URN" \[[RFC3305](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3305)\].
